questions.help:
Road traffic collisions    
   
2 Road traffic collisions can be avoided
With thought and knowledge it is possible to work out where, when, how and why collisions occur and therefore how to avoid them.
Certain circumstances related to the vehicle, the road and the environment but above all the driver, increase the likelihood of a road traffic collision or make the results of a collision much more serious. These circumstances are called “risk factors” and avoiding or minimising them reduces the possibility of being involved in a collision.
Some of these risk factors are fatigue, alcohol, excessive speed, ice or driving with a poorly maintained vehicle, particularly worn tyres.
(Página 249 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
ILLNESS AND MEDICATION  
   
19 The consequences of illnesses and drugs in traffic collisions
To drive a vehicle requires certain conditions relating to the physical and mental aptitude of the driver to be initially satisfied and thereafter maintained. It is therefore necessary to go to a designated medical centre for drivers who will verify whether there is a serious impediment to the applicant or driver, which will prevent them performing this task safely.
A mild illness does not have to exclude driving, although it can reduce the ability to drive safely (for example, a common cold can cause sleepiness and loss of concentration). Therefore, you should always ask your doctor about the precautions to be taken before driving, especially if you have a chronic illness.
(Página 46 del manual 'Learning to drive')

7 Tunnels and underpasses
7.1 Stopping in tunnels or underpasses
If, whilst inside a tunnel or underpass, a vehicle is forced to stop due to traffic congestion and because of other stationary vehicles, the occupants of the vehicle mustn’t leave the vehicle. The driver must put on his hazard warning lights (temporarily) to inform the drivers that travel behind him of the situation. He should also keep illuminated the position lights (side lights) but turn off the engine. All drivers must stop as far as possible away from the vehicle in front -extend their safety distance.

8.1 Obligatory requirements regarding rear-view mirrors

A rear-view interior mirror. This must comply with the field of vision in accordance with the regulations. Certain groups of road users are more at risk because of their characteristics and are more likely to become a casualty.

Among the drivers most at risk, are young people, older people and the drivers of two-wheeled vehicles (bicycles, motorcycles and mopeds), because in the event of an accident they are more likely to be injured or die.

Speed by itself does not necessarily constitute a risk factor. However, driving at a high speed makes it difficult for the driver to control the vehicle in a situation should the need arise.

5 Overtaking
5.8 Situations when you must not overtake  
Specifically, it is prohibited to overtake:
In any place or circumstance where visibility is not sufficient to be able to complete the manoeuvre or abort it once started, unless the two directions of traffic are clearly marked out and the manoeuvre can be completed without moving into the zone reserved for the opposite direction, specifically:
- On bends and changes in gradient with reduced visibility.
- When the weather conditions significantly reduce visibility (fog, heavy rain or when the sun is low, dazzling drivers). In these circumstances, you should never overtake.
- Behind a vehicle which is also overtaking if, due to its size or other features, it prevents the vehicle’s driver from seeing the road ahead.
(Página 191 del manual 'Learning to drive')
